raw_case_text:
A 59-year-old man with systemic arterial hypertension and a history of cigarette smoking from ages 15 to 19 years (approximately one pack per day, ~4 pack-years) was under outpatient follow-up for low-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (Gleason 6, ISUP 1). During routine preoperative assessment for urological surgery, he reported mild exertional dyspnea consistent with New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional Class II, prompting further cardiovascular evaluation.
A comprehensive social and infectious risk assessment revealed no history of high-risk sexual practices, illicit drug use, or prior sexually transmitted infections. He reported a monogamous relationship for more than two decades and no family history of syphilis or congenital infection. These details guided interpretation of the serologic findings, supporting late latent or tertiary syphilis rather than recent exposure.
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) angiography demonstrated a giant aneurysm primarily involving the aortic arch, measuring 114 x 94 x 93 mm, with a longitudinal extension of 79 mm. Additional dilatations were observed in the midascending aorta (49 x 48 mm), distal aortic arch (31 x 28 mm), and proximal descending thoracic aorta (26 x 25 mm) (Figures 1 and 2). The aneurysm morphology and maximal diameter indicated a high risk of rupture, leading to urgent referral for surgical management.
Serologic evaluation confirmed active syphilitic infection, with VDRL 1:32, TPHA positive, and negative HIV screening. The hepatitis panel revealed HBsAg negative, anti-HBc IgM negative, protective anti-HBs titers, and anti-HCV negative, excluding viral hepatitis-related vasculopathy. The patient completed a full course of benzathine penicillin G, 2.4 million units intramuscularly once weekly for three consecutive weeks, consistent with the CDC and WHO recommendations for late latent/tertiary syphilis.
The procedure was performed via median sternotomy. The ascending aorta and entire aortic arch were replaced using a 28 mm x 30 cm Dacron graft (Figure 3). Deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) was instituted at a core temperature of 20 C, with a total circulatory arrest time of 35 min. Selective antegrade cerebral perfusion (SACP) was delivered via cannulation of the brachiocephalic trunk throughout the arrest period. The supraaortic trunks were reimplanted en bloc into the graft using the island technique. Cardiopulmonary bypass time was 2 h and 23 min, and aortic crossclamp time was 1 h and 55 min.
The postoperative course was complicated by a left pleural effusion requiring therapeutic thoracentesis and by transient delirium with upper limb myoclonus. Neurological evaluation and imaging revealed no structural abnormalities, and symptoms resolved fully with supportive care.
Histopathologic examination demonstrated advanced atherosclerotic changes with dystrophic calcification, along with inflammatory infiltrates affecting the vasa vasorum, consistent with syphilitic aortitis. This mixed pattern suggests coexistence of chronic infectious aortitis with degenerative aortic disease.
At two-month follow-up, the patient exhibited complete clinical recovery, with improvement in anemia, resolution of chest discomfort, and full restoration of functional capacity. VDRL titers decreased from 1:32 to 1:8, indicating appropriate serologic response. Continued outpatient surveillance with periodic imaging was planned.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 59-year-old man presented during routine preoperative urological evaluation with mild exertional dyspnea (NYHA functional Class II).
subjective.history_of_present_illness: While undergoing routine preoperative assessment for low-risk prostate adenocarcinoma (Gleason 6, ISUP grade 1), the patient reported mild exertional dyspnea corresponding to NYHA Class II, prompting cardiovascular imaging.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of systemic arterial hypertension, low-risk prostate adenocarcinoma, and remote adolescent cigarette smoking (1 pack/day from ages 15 to 19, ~4 pack-years). Reported a monogamous relationship for >20 years with no history of prior STIs, high-risk sexual behavior, illicit drug use, or family history of syphilis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mild exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort.

objective.physical_examination: Cardiovascular functional status was NYHA Class II.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV screening and viral hepatitis panel (HBsAg negative, anti-HBc IgM negative, protective anti-HBs positive, anti-HCV negative) were negative for active co-infection.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced chest CT angiography revealed a giant aneurysm of the aortic arch measuring 114 x 94 x 93 mm (longitudinal extension 79 mm), alongside ectasia/dilatation of the mid-ascending aorta (49 x 48 mm), distal aortic arch (31 x 28 mm), and proximal descending thoracic aorta (26 x 25 mm). Histopathology of the resected aortic wall demonstrated inflammatory infiltrates targeting the vasa vasorum consistent with syphilitic aortitis superimposed on advanced atherosclerotic changes with dystrophic calcification.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed tertiary cardiovascular syphilis presenting with syphilitic aortitis and a giant aortic arch aneurysm, established via reactive serum VDRL (titer 1:32), positive TPHA, and characteristic vasa vasorum endarteritis/aortitis on aortic histopathology. Treated preoperatively with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units once weekly for 3 consecutive weeks, followed by median sternotomy replacement of the ascending aorta and total aortic arch using a 28 mm x 30 cm Dacron graft with en bloc island reimplantation of the supra-aortic trunks under deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (20 C, 35 min) and selective antegrade cerebral perfusion. Transient postoperative delirium/myoclonus and a left pleural effusion resolved with thoracentesis and supportive care, and at 2-month follow-up he had full functional recovery with a fourfold decline in VDRL titer from 1:32 to 1:8.
